brief: A chart-roundup note juxtaposing current market extremes against Q4 2018, reporting rather than arguing a thesis. The S&P 500 closed more than 4 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average, an extremity last seen August 25, 2015 (Bespoke). The one-week move in VIX was the fifth-largest on record (GS vol desk). An SPX overlay recalls that VIX closed above 36 on Christmas Eve 2018, the same day the S&P 500 made its closing low (GS). On positioning, Hedge Fund VIP stocks' recent drawdown is among the worst on record (Goldman); US single stocks were shorted every day this week, the largest weekly shorting activity since June 2022 and third-largest in the past decade (GS Prime); hedge fund leverage's decline from 12-month highs now matches some of the most extreme deleveraging episodes since 2018 (JPM Prime); and US hedge fund net and gross exposure are both at the zero percentile over the trailing 12 months (Morgan Stanley Prime Brokerage). Separately, gold is in its biggest drawdown since the 1980s (Morgan Stanley). The note lines these stats up under a 2018-echo framing but draws no explicit forecast or trade call.
